frames.narration: A creator uploads a 20-minute video. The app sends it in chunks, so if the connection breaks it resumes from the last chunk instead of starting again.
The API writes the original file to object storage, tells the creator it is safe, and puts a transcode job on the queue. The creator is free to leave.
A transcoder takes the job, reads the original and writes it back as four-second segments in several qualities, from 240p to 1080p. A crash would just rerun the job, because segment names are fixed.
When every quality is written, the video is marked ready and its manifest is published. Only now can anyone watch it.
A viewer presses play. The player asks the API for the video's manifest, a small list of qualities and segment addresses.
The player starts cautiously with the first segment at 480p, requested from the nearest CDN cache. This cache has never seen it, so it fetches it from storage, keeps a copy and passes it on.
The segment arrived quickly, so the player asks for 1080p next. The connection then drops and segment 3 comes slowly, so it falls back to 360p instead of freezing.
A neighbour starts the same video. The segment is already in the same cache, so it is a hit: no trip to storage, and a faster start.
